source.text: Use USWDS color tokens, and avoid custom colors whenever possible.
Grade is a way to express how light or dark a color is. USWDS uses a 100-point scale to communicate a color token's grade, where 0 is pure white and 100 is pure black.
We've regularized these grades across color families; a color of grade 50 in one color family should be the same level of lightness as a color of grade 50 in another color family.
Section 508, which aligns with WCAG 2.0 Level AA, sets the legal standard for the needed contrast level between text and its background.
The baseline AA contrast standard is 4.5:1 for most text and 3:1 for large text (19px+ bold or 24px+ normal text).
Each color family has 10 grades, which fall between 5 and 90. Pure white is the equivalent of grade 0, and pure black is the equivalent of grade 100.
We call the difference in grade between any two colors the magic number.
A magic number of 40+ results in WCAG 2.0 AA Large Text contrast (example: gray-90 and indigo-warm-50v).
A magic number of 50+ results in WCAG 2.0 AA contrast or AAA Large Text contrast (example: gray-90 and red-40).
A magic number of 70+ results in WCAG 2.0 AAA contrast (example: gray-10 and red-80).
Colors of grade 50 result in Section 508 AA contrast against both pure white (grade 0) and pure black (grade 100).
Use magic numbers to choose accessible color combinations from any palette and color family.
Avoiding pure black text on a white background helps dyslexia, Irlen Syndrome, light sensitivity, and autism.
Don't use color exclusively to convey meaning.
Each theme token is drawn from a system color token and we only use token-based colors in official components.
Base is a project's neutral color, typically some tint of gray, and usually used as the text color throughout.

Primary, secondary, and accent colors can be thought of as falling into a proportional 60/30/10 relationship: about 60% of your site's color would be the primary color family, about 30% would be the secondary color family, and about 10% would be the accent color families.
System color family gray-cool: 1 #fbfcfd, 2 #f7f9fa, 3 #f5f6f7, 4 #f1f3f6, 5 #edeff0, 10 #dfe1e2, 20 #c6cace, 30 #a9aeb1, 40 #8d9297, 50 #71767a, 60 #565c65, 70 #3d4551, 80 #2d2e2f, 90 #1c1d1f.
Any spacing value in utilities or component CSS should use the following spacing unit tokens, based on multiples of 8px.
The USWDS typescale includes nine regularized theme tokens drawn from 21 system tokens.
If your project requires more than nine sizes, use system size tokens as needed.
Theme size tokens: 3xs = system 2, 2xs = system 3, xs = system 4, sm = system 5, md = system 6, lg = system 9, xl = system 12, 2xl = system 14, 3xl = system 15.
Typefaces vary in optical size. At any specific pixel value, an optically small typeface like Source Sans Pro will appear smaller than an optically large typeface like Merriweather.
To make different typefaces appear the same size (here called the target size) at each step of the scale, the absolute size of each token's output varies depending on the font family.

Normalization (final output = target size x normalization): Georgia: 1.05; Helvetica: 1.01; Merriweather: 0.98; Open Sans: 1.01; Public Sans: 1.00; Roboto Mono: 0.95; Source Sans Pro: 1.06; System fonts: 1.00; Tahoma: 1.00; Verdana: 0.99.
USWDS available fonts: Georgia, Helvetica, Merriweather, Open Sans, Public Sans, Roboto Mono, Source Sans Pro, Tahoma, Verdana, and system fonts.
Use buttons for the most important actions you want users to take on your site, such as Download, Sign up or Log out.
Use standard buttons for actions that go a next step.
Use outline buttons for actions that happen on the current page.
Give an important action a distinctive style. Style the button most users should select in a way that distinguishes it from other buttons on the page.
Avoid using too many buttons on a page.
Use sentence-case capitalization for button labels.
Keep button text short. Button text should be as short as possible with action words that clearly explain what will happen when the button is selected.
Lead with a verb. Make the first word of the button's text a verb. For example, instead of Complaint filing, label the button File a complaint.
Buttons should display a visible focus state when users tab to them.
Keep unavailable actions understandable. Explain why an action is unavailable and how to make it available.
Font names in CSS (stack names): Merriweather is served as Merriweather Web; Public Sans is served as Public Sans Web; Roboto Mono is served as Roboto Mono Web.

rules.why: 'Avoid custom colors whenever possible' is read as a failure for any colour outside the system tokens (white and black are grades 0 and 100, U6).
rules.formal: every text, background and border colour is a system colour token, white or black
text contrast against its effective background >= 4.5:1
large text (>= 24 px, or >= 19 px and bold): contrast >= 3:1

rules.why: U13 gives a reason to avoid pure black on white; we read it as a failure.
rules.formal: no text is pure black (#000000) on pure white (#ffffff)
every margin and padding is a spacing unit token (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 120 px)

rules.why: Sizes are target x normalization; the multiples in U51 are rounded to two decimals, so a size within 0.6% (or 0.1 px) of target x multiple is accepted.
rules.formal: font size = a system size token's target x the font's normalization
the font is one of the USWDS available fonts or the system font
button labels are in sentence case

rules.why: 'A verb' is checked against a list of common interface verbs (a proxy).
rules.formal: the first word of a button label is a verb

rules.why: 'Too many' is not defined; we set 5. Never planted as a violation, and not asked of the models.
'Short' is not defined; we set 4 words. Never planted as a violation, and not asked of the models.
rules.formal: a button label has at most 4 words

residue.reason: advice on choosing colours, not a page requirement (its arithmetic is checked as a claim, see ruler)
judgment: whether colour is the only signal
judgment: 'can be thought of'; an area proportion, outside this slice
judgment: which actions are the most important
judgment: whether an action goes a next step
judgment: whether an action happens on the current page
judgment: which action most users should select
invisible in a static render: focus states
judgment: whether an explanation is given
